Deutsche Bank
For 2023 Placement
Gauri Shewale
Final Year BTech Computer Engineering Student 2019-2023
Deutsche Bank visited our campus in July end 2022 to hire final year students for the
role of Graduate Technical Analyst in Technology Data and Innovation (TDI) Business
Division.
Their criteria was:
●CPI : 7 and above
●
Branches : Computers, IT & EXTC (Electronics and Telecommunication).
There were 5 rounds conducted overall.
1.
Online Coding Test.
2. Technical Round-1.
3. Technical Round-2.
4. Professional-fitment Round.
5. HR Round.

Round 1
(27th July, 2022)    (1.5 hrs)
It was an online test on HackerEarth platform. There were 3 coding questions in this
round. The questions were of easy-medium difficulty. The scores for questions were
20,50,50 respectively. There were marks for partial test cases.
Coding Questions-
1) Armstrong Number
Check whether input number is Armstrong or not
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/program-for-armstrong-numbers/
Example 1) :
Input:
153
Output:     YES  - - - - [:. 13 + 33 + 53 = 153 ] N =3
Example 2) :
Input:      1224
Output:    NO  - - - - - [ :. 14 + 24 + 24 + 44 != 1224 ]
2) Given two arrays A [a1,.......,an] and B[b1,.....,bn],  print the minimum number of
moves to make two arrays equal noting that you must make
Ai = Ai + 2 & Aj =Aj - 2  . . . . . . . 0<=i < n  in one move
Example 1) :
Input:
A = [2,5,6] , B = [1,2,10]
Output:     2
Explanation:
Move 1) In array A, we modify (2,3) indices [considering 1-based indexing]
So A = [2, 5 -2, 6+2] = [2,3,8]
Move 2) In array A, we modify (2,3) indices [considering 1-based indexing]
So A = [2, 3 -2, 8+2] = [2,1,10]
Example 2) :
Input:
A = [0,2,8] , B = [2,4,6]
Output:     -1
Explanation:
It is not possible to make both the arrays equal using the given rule.

3) Consider that you have been given the current state of a parking lot such that
numbers > 1 stand for a car, -1 stands for a pillar, and 0 stands for an empty parking
space. Basically, print the number of steps to get Desired Array from the current
array considering you can move forwards or backwards in ‘0’ place i.e empty
parking space.
Note: You can’t move pillars with empty parking space.
Example 1):
Input:
Current_array = [-1,1,0,2] , Desired_array = [-1,1,2,0]
Output:     1
Example 2):
Input:
Current_array = [-1,8,0,6,7,4,0,2] , Desired_array = [-1,8,6,7,2,4,0,0]
Output:     -1
I was able to solve the first coding question completely, the second question partially
(half test cases passed) and in the third one just the sample test cases.
29 Students were shortlisted from the online test for the next round. There was a
Pre-Placement Talk on 2nd August from 2pm to 3pm on Skype for the shortlisted
candidates. Here, they introduced us to the organization structure, tech stack, projects,
values and details about Deutsche Bank.

3rd August, 2022
All the interviews were held offline. So we were supposed to reach TPO seminar hall at
9am in formals with resume copies.
Round 2
(Interview)   (Technical Round-1)  (1hr)
The interviewer introduced herself and asked me to do the same.  She went over each
section of my resume and basically grilled me on it. (DONT LIE ON YOUR RESUME ever).
She asked me the following questions:
1)
Elaborate on work done in my AWS summer internship.
2) My projects involved React Js, so she asked me about React Hooks,
asynchronous functions, etc
3) OOPS
4) https://leetcode.com/problems/binary-tree-right-side-view/ (with pseudocode on
paper)
5) Normalization in databases and their forms
6) Indexing in databases
7) Difference between a primary key,  unique key, candidate key
8) Given a table which has ID and position of employees, write an SQL query to
a) Find IDs which are having positions as “analyst”/ “associate”/ “manager”
b) Count IDs per position and arrange them in descending order of count
value
9) Find the length of maximum sequence of continuous 1’s formed by replacing
at-most k zeroes by ones  (with pseudocode on paper)
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/longest-subsegment-1s-formed-changing-k-0s/
She then asked me if I had any questions for her. I asked her about her
experience at Deutsche bank so far and what sets DB apart from the other banks.
Round 3
(Interview)    (Technical Round-2)    (~1hr)
1)
Introduce yourself.
2) pandas vs numpy
3) How would you read a csv file? - ( Write the code on paper)

4) Demonstrate addition of new rows / columns in Dataframe
5) Doubly linked list and real life example
6) Different types of Joins in SQL
a) Given a table A containing Id and table B containing Id and another column
perform full join, left join, right join, full join and explain the output.
7) SQL query to find the third highest salary
8) A flow chart of one basic question
9) High level design of an application for sports community
10) Elaborate on work done in my summer internship
11) Why DB?
He then asked me if I had any questions for him. I asked him about his experience
at Deutsche bank so far and work - life balance at DB.
Round 4
(Professional Fitness)    (~30 mins)
1) Introduce yourself.
2) Tell me about a challenge you faced and how you resolved it.
3) What do you wish to explore? ( I replied with Blockchain technology -> Follow up
question: What do you know about blockchain? )
4) How does international money transfer take place via banks? (SWIFT Banking
system)
5) Consider a scenario where you and your team are having a group discussion on a
project but the senior people in your team dismiss your suggested solution
without proper reason. What will you do in this case?
6) Consider a case where you work on a project and deploy it to production. Now a
bug arises in the code while in production which is causing some impact on the
business of the company. You are called over the weekend to investigate the
issue. You find that you can either provide a quick fix for the bug in two days or
provide a proper fix for the bug in 3-4 weeks. What will you do in this situation?
7) Elaborate on work done in my Summer Internship

He then asked me if I had any questions for him. I asked him about his experience
at Deutsche bank so far and what was the process of onboarding for a freshly
graduated FTE.
Everyone who gave the ProFit round was asked to give the HR round as well.
Round 5
(HR)    (20-30 mins)
1) Introduce yourself
2) How was your day till now? Are you tired?
3) Family Background
4) Hobbies / things other than academics
5) How does a bank make money?
6) If you see your colleagues are doing some things which are against the company
policies / can harm the company, what will you do?
7) How do you keep yourself updated with current affairs?
8) How will you handle an underperformer in your team?
9) Why DB?
10) What will I choose if I get a PPO at my summer internship company as well as DB
offer?
He then asked me if I had any questions for him. I asked him about his experience
at Deutsche Bank so far.
The interviews concluded around 6 PM and we got the results within an hour. All the 12
candidates who gave the Pro-Fit and HR round were selected and I was lucky to be one
among them (✿◠‿◠)

RESOURCES:
1)
Interview Prep (Amazing repository made by our senior Yash Jain)
2) Leetcode, Interview bit
3) https://crack-oop-system-design.herokuapp.com/
(Awesome documentation made by our senior Palak Mantry)
4) Geeks for geeks
5) Prep Doc
SOME TIPS:
●
DO NOT EVER LIE ON YOUR RESUME. The interviewers have seen hundreds of
students before you and you will get caught because they will grill you on that. Be
thorough with your resume for questions like why a particular
technology/framework was used by you instead of another one, difference
between usage of those frameworks, etc.
●
In interviews, start with a brute force approach and then proceed to the optimal
solution even if you know the optimal solution perfectly.  This helps you in getting
the hang of the problem and the interviewer gets to know that you did try to
understand the process of reaching your final solution. There will be follow-up
questions based on your answer (like on data structures used..etc) so be
prepared.
●
REMEMBER THAT THE INTERVIEWER IS NOT YOUR ENEMY.  Ask for clarifications
regarding problems. They will try to give you a lot of hints to solve the problems.
●
THINK OUT LOUD.  The interviewers are not mind readers... so talk. Tell them
honestly even if you are not sure about your solution. IT IS OKAY to tell them if
you don’t know everything or you are not able to solve the problem completely.
Your approach and way of thinking is judged mostly. (Silence here won’t help you)
●
Always have a look at some interview experiences beforehand. Checkout Geeks
For Geeks and COC drive. Very Helpful.
●
PRACTICE YOUR TECHNICAL INTRODUCTION. Seems like a very obvious thing
but at that moment when you are nervous and remember social awkwardness,
you tend to miss out things about yourself. Practice in front of a mirror.
●
Don’t neglect your CS fundamentals.

●
DON’T FORGET TO RESEARCH ABOUT THE COMPANY. The interviewer will
probably ask you about the company’s mission, vision, principles or what it does.
(HR rounds guaranteed)
●
Prepare for behavioral questions too. We generally study technical questions and
completely ignore behavioral questions.
●
ALWAYS ASK the interviewer something when they ask you whether you have any
questions for them.  It shows that you do have interest in the company.
●
Keep some hard copies of your resume handy. Since some companies take offline
interviews, they do ask for hard copies.
●
Stay hydrated and eat food properly on interview day as the entire process is
hectic.
●
Stay Calm and focused during the interviews and the entire process. Things don’t
always go the way you wished them to. Don’t lose hope. Don’t Give Up. EVER.
Remember your body language communicates as well as your mouth.
If you have any queries, feel free to drop an email at gaurishewale08@gmail.com
All the best!  You can do it! (✿^‿^ )
